title: Uniform, reservoir, stratified
summary: Three ways to draw a sample, including from a stream.

choices.text: Stratified sampling draws inside predefined groups (a class label, a region) so a rare group is not missing from a small sample purely by chance. The draw can be proportional to the group or can deliberately oversample it.
A simple random sample of a finite table gives every row the same inclusion probability.
Reservoir sampling upweights the most recent items, the way an exponential moving average does.
Reservoir sampling keeps a uniform sample of size k from a stream whose length you do not know in advance. After t items have arrived, each of those t items is equally likely to be in the reservoir.
